samples.summary: The new `getStore()` proxy creates a *second* page-setup write path with different post-write semantics than `writePageSetup`, violating the documented single-write-path invariant
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2901-2912) writes `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` but deliberately skips `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()` and `render()` — all four of which `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) performs. Any caller reaching the write through the public `getStore()` handle (the export button at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:53, the find bar at docs-find-bar.tsx:56 and the hunt bridge at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386 already hold that handle) therefore persists geometry into the store/CRDT while the editor keeps a stale cached `Doc._document` and layout; the very next ruler drag re-reads the stale value at editor.ts:2094 (`resolvePageSetup(doc.document.pageSetup)`) and writes it back, silently reverting the store write. The design doc that this branch updated still asserts the opposite invariant: docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:350 — "there is no second way to write a page setup". Fix belongs on the new code: either have the proxy delegate to `writePageSetup`, or drop the store-level door entirely.

samples.summary: The dialog's own margin validation is looser than the new `assertUsablePageSetup` floor, so an accepted form can hit an uncaught `RangeError` from the newly-throwing `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`
samples.evidence: `docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx` gates Apply on `parsed.left! + parsed.right! >= pageWidth` (content must merely be > 0), then calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` at line 154 with no try/catch. The engine's new guard `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1000) requires `margins.left + margins.right <= width - MIN_CONTENT_PX` (content >= 1 px). For a document whose stored `paperSize` is a non-integer custom width — reachable via a collaborator's CRDT write, or via `resolvePageSetup`'s new proportional `fitMargins` scaling which produces fractional lengths — a content box of e.g. 0.5 px passes the dialog and throws inside the submit handler, which React surfaces as an unhandled error rather than a form message. Either share `MIN_CONTENT_PX` with the dialog or catch the `RangeError` at the call site.

samples.summary: Design doc still states the old `resolvePageSetup` contract (pure defaulting), which this change turns into the sanitisation/clamping boundary
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:96-97: "A helper `resolvePageSetup(setup: PageSetup | undefined): PageSetup` returns `setup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` (callers pass `doc.document.pageSetup`)." After this diff (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:826) it also coerces non-finite/negative/zero dimensions to defaults, coerces orientation, and proportionally shrinks margins to keep a `MIN_CONTENT_PX` content box — the contract every consumer (exporters, CLI pagination, `MemDocStore`, `YorkieDocStore`) now relies on. This file sits under docs/design/<topic>/, which the enforced backtick-resolution check does not recurse into, so nothing else will flag it.

finding.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2901-2912) writes `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` but deliberately skips `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()` and `render()` — all four of which `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) performs. Any caller reaching the write through the public `getStore()` handle (the export button at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:53, the find bar at docs-find-bar.tsx:56 and the hunt bridge at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386 already hold that handle) therefore persists geometry into the store/CRDT while the editor keeps a stale cached `Doc._document` and layout; the very next ruler drag re-reads the stale value at editor.ts:2094 (`resolvePageSetup(doc.document.pageSetup)`) and writes it back, silently reverting the store write. verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted (editor.ts:2900-2912 skips snapshot/refresh/invalidateLayout/render that writePageSetup at editor.ts:2078-2090 performs), but the finding fails the blast-radius bar: there is no broken or bypassing call site. A repo-wide grep of `setPageSetup(` shows the only production writers are editor.setPageSetup from the dialog (docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:154) and the ruler drag (editor.ts:2093-2097), both routed through writePageSetup; the only callers of getStore().setPageSetup are two tests (editor-page-setup.test.ts:341,347; editor-read-only.test.ts:332). The three sites the finding names as reaching the write do not call it at all — docs-export-button.tsx:53 calls getDocument(), docs-find-bar.tsx:56 calls snapshot(), harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386 calls canUndo(). No guard is bypassed either: assertUsablePageSetup and the readOnly drop ARE applied on the proxy path; what differs is repaint bookkeeping, and that door predates the proxy (getStore() previously handed out the raw DocStore, per docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:145-159). The residue is logic inside the new function plus a design-doc mismatch (docs-pagination.md:350) — the correctness lens's lane (it raised it as minor, .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:7) and design-fit's, not this one.

finding.summary: `EditorAPI.getDoc()` hands out a `Doc` that writes straight through to the unguarded store — a second door beside the one this delta closed
finding.evidence: `getDoc: () => doc` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2925 region, unchanged) returns the `Doc` model, which holds `private store: DocStore` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:98) pointing at the raw `docStore`, not the new `guardedStore`. `Doc.applyBlockStyle` (document.ts:599-600) delegates directly to `this.store.applyBlockStyle`, as do `insertText`, `deleteText`, `deleteBlock`, `insertBlockAfter`, `insertRow`, `mergeCells`, etc. (document.ts:260-1069). So `editor.getDoc().applyBlockStyle(...)` reaches the same CRDT write in read-only mode, past both the MUTATING_METHODS neutering (editor.ts:3959) and the new `getStore()` proxy. `getDoc()` is already used from the frontend (e.g. packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:323 and frontend consumers), so the accessor is live.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: `const doc = new Doc(docStore)` (editor.ts:1039) binds the model to the RAW store, and `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:2933) publishes it on the public EditorAPI (editor.ts:53). `Doc` holds `private store: DocStore` (document.ts:98) and forwards mutations untouched — insertText (document.ts:260-261), applyBlockStyle (document.ts:599-600), deleteBlock (document.ts:627-628). Neither the read-only MUTATING_METHODS neutering (editor.ts:3978-3995, which only rewrites members of `api`, and does not list `getDoc`) nor the new `pageSetupGuardedStore` proxy (editor.ts:2913-2929) is on that path. The bypass is not merely theoretical: docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57 builds `new FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), ...)`, whose replace path writes via `this.doc.deleteText/insertText` (find-replace.ts:79-83) from handlers at docs-find-bar.tsx:115-129; docs-view.tsx:599-606 renders DocsFindBar with no `readOnly` prop while every sibling component there receives one (597, 610, 618, 628). Refutation grounds all fail: the code is present as described (not `not-present`); nothing guards the Doc path (not `already-guarded`); and a reachable bypass of a guard is explicitly this lens's lane (not `out-of-scope`). In-repo text (editor.ts:2875-2883, editor-read-only.test.ts:341-359, docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:145-159) declares this deferred to "issue #989", but repository prose cannot set the rubric, and pre-existing status is not a refutation ground.
